model.name: Commercial Contract
model.purpose: Capture agreements between parties as jointly owned multi-party records: formation and consent, the instrument and its clauses, the obligations and schedule those clauses create, performance and exemption, amendment, breach, remedy and termination, plus the contractual terms that govern notices, transfer and dispute forum without absorbing those sibling domains.
model.scope_statement: This model describes commercial, including international commercial, contracts in which each party acts in the exercise of its trade or profession. It covers how a binding agreement is formed, how the agreed text is structured and interpreted, what duties and times for performance it creates, how performance, non-performance and agreed change are recorded, and how the shared record is identified, evidenced and disclosed. It is format-neutral: JSON, XML, PDF, paper counterparts, EDI messages and ledger entries are projections of the same semantics. It aligns to CISG for international sales of goods, UNIDROIT PICC 2016 for general commercial contract rules, LegalRuleML for deontic markup, Akoma Ntoso for legal-document identity and hierarchy, the HCCH Principles for choice of law, UCC § 2-201 for a competing writing rule, and UNCITRAL electronic commerce and signature model laws for functional equivalence of electronic records. It does not itself determine capacity of natural persons, proprietary effects, insolvency treatment, or the procedure of a court or tribunal.
in_scope: Identity, versions and classification of a commercial agreement as a legal instrument and as a joint record
Party positions, roles, places of business and signing capacity as they appear in the agreement
Offer, invitation to treat, acceptance, rejection, counter-offer, withdrawal, revocation, late acceptance and formation by conduct, including automated or EDI contracting
Battle of forms, writings in confirmation, terms deliberately left open, and conditions that the contract exist only in a particular form
Writing, signature, electronic record and electronic signature requirements, and reservations that restore a writing rule
Hierarchical clause structure, standard terms versus negotiated terms, entire-agreement and no-oral-modification clauses
Interpretation from party intent, reasonable-person meaning, usages, practices and subsequent conduct
Deontic commitments: obligations, permissions, prohibitions, rights, conditions, warranties and representations arising from clauses
Time, place and manner of performance, milestones, instalments, price, currency and payment mechanics
Delivery, examination, conformity, acceptance, rejection, cure and performance evidence
Passing of risk, impediment, force majeure, hardship and related notices
Amendment, waiver, estoppel against a form clause, assignment, novation, guarantee and third-party beneficiary terms

Breach including fundamental and anticipatory breach, additional time to perform, suspension, adequate assurance, damages, price reduction, interest, specific performance, penalties or liquidated damages, avoidance or termination, restitution and surviving clauses
Limitation or prescription of actions as a contract-adjacent time bar
Choice of law, including dépeçage and choice of non-State rules of law, and contractual dispute-resolution clauses as terms
Notices, confidentiality, counterparts, content hashes, joint-record mirrors, consented status disclosure and adjudication access
out_of_scope: The legal person or natural person as an entity: those belong to organization and person sibling models; this model holds only the party position and a referent link
Internal corporate authority, board powers and constitutional documents except as a referenced check on signing capacity
Public procurement process, tendering, award criteria and standstill: an award may compose into a new agreement here but the process lives in procurement
Insurance as a specialised underwriting product: a policy may extend this model rather than be modelled as a generic commercial contract
Price indices, market observations and valuation methodology: an executed agreement may be a price observation source under a separate contribution contract
Court, arbitral or mediation procedure, evidence rules, recognition and enforcement of awards: only the contractual clause selecting forum, seat, rules and language is in scope
Consumer contracts, household sales and individual employment contracts
Validity grounds such as mistake, fraud, duress, unconscionability and illegality as a full doctrine set: CISG does not govern validity; national validity remains a sibling or overlay
Proprietary effects, passing of title, security interests and third-party in rem rights
Insolvency stay, claw-back, administrator election and ipso facto treatment
External agency power to bind a principal to a third party
Tax, customs, sanctions lists and regulatory licences as public-law regimes, except as contractual conditions or impediments referenced from the agreement
Stewardship policy, access-grant objects and generic audit-trail mechanics except as mixed in or referenced

boundary_notes.distinction: A commercial contract is not an organization; it is a jointly owned multi-party record that binds party positions

CISG applies to contracts of sale of goods between parties with places of business in different States and does not apply to consumer sales, securities, ships, electricity, preponderant services, seller death-or-injury liability, validity or property effects

boundary_notes.neighbor: UNIDROIT Principles of International Commercial Contracts
boundary_notes.distinction: UNIDROIT PICC apply when chosen, when used to interpret or supplement international instruments or domestic law, or as lex mercatoria; they are not a State statute

boundary_notes.neighbor: HCCH Principles on Choice of Law
boundary_notes.distinction: HCCH Principles apply to international commercial contracts and expressly exclude consumer and employment contracts, capacity, arbitration and choice-of-court agreements as such, companies and trusts, insolvency, proprietary effects and external agency
Choice of court and arbitration agreements are contractual terms here; the process of hearing a dispute is a sibling dispute-resolution model
Standard-form industry contracts such as ISDA, FIDIC or GAFTA are profiles or extensions, not a second core model

Smart-contract code may evidence or automate performance but is not, without more, a legal agreement; automated contracting is in scope only to the extent UNIDROIT Article 2.1.1 comment 3 describes self-executing electronic actions agreed by the parties

layers.name: Agreement identity and versions
layers.description: Assign master identifiers and distinguish abstract agreement, textual version, signed manifestation and stored item.

findings.name: Agreement identity and FRBR levels
findings.description: Akoma Ntoso requires persistent URI/IRI identification and separates FRBR Work (the abstract legal resource), Expression (a version whose content differs by language or amendment), Manifestation (a format such as XML or PDF) and Item (a stored copy). A commercial agreement needs the same split so that an amending instrument, a convenience translation and a hashed PDF counterpart are not treated as different contracts. A date is not an identifier. The adopting Dimension may add a UUID or ULID only after an authoritative master-system identifier and any governed IRI are recorded.

questions.text: What is the authoritative master-system identifier of this agreement, which system minted it, and what governed IRI or Dimension UUID or ULID is attached if the master id is absent or not globally unique?
Which FRBR level is being operated on: the abstract agreement, a particular amended or language expression, a signed manifestation, or a stored item, and how do those levels link?
What content hash and counterpart grouping identify the exact signed or otherwise authentic text so that later projections can be checked without treating a copy as a new agreement?
Which agent or system first registered this identity, at what observation or ingestion time, and is that distinct from the legal execution event time?

layers.name: Classification and applicable law
layers.description: Classify the contract type and record the law or rules of law that govern it, including overriding mandatory rules.

findings.name: Subject-matter class and CISG sphere
findings.description: CISG Article 1 applies the Convention to contracts of sale of goods between parties with places of business in different States when those States are Contracting States or private international law leads to a Contracting State. Articles 2–5 exclude consumer goods, auctions, execution sales, securities, ships, electricity, preponderant labour or services, validity, property effects and death or personal injury. Article 6 allows parties to exclude or derogate from the Convention. UNIDROIT PICC cover commercial contracts more broadly than sales. Classification therefore decides whether CISG, PICC, a domestic code or a specialised extension such as insurance is the right alignment, and must not treat a services-preponderant or consumer deal as an in-scope CISG sale.

questions.text: What is the contract type and subject-matter class, and is the preponderant obligation a sale of goods, a supply of services or labour, or another commercial class such as licence, loan or distribution?
Do the parties have places of business in different States such that CISG Article 1 is engaged, have the parties excluded CISG under Article 6, and do any Article 2–5 exclusions apply?
Is each party acting in the exercise of its trade or profession, and is the contract therefore outside consumer and employment regimes that this model excludes?

findings.name: Choice of law, rules of law and mandatory limits
findings.description: HCCH Principles Article 2 provide that a contract is governed by the law chosen by the parties; the choice may cover the whole or part of the contract, may assign different laws to different parts, may be made or modified at any time without prejudicing formal validity or third-party rights, and needs no connection to the parties or the transaction. Article 3 allows generally accepted neutral and balanced non-State rules of law such as the UNIDROIT Principles unless forum law forbids that choice in court. Article 1(3) keeps capacity, arbitration and choice-of-court agreements, companies and trusts, insolvency, proprietary effects and external agency outside the Principles. Overriding mandatory rules and public policy remain limits. CISG Article 7 requires regard to international character, uniformity and good faith, with gap-filling first from CISG general principles then from the law applicable under private international law.

questions.text: Which State law or generally accepted rules of law did the parties choose, was the choice express or tacit, and does it apply to the whole contract or to identified parts?
Was the choice of law made or modified after conclusion, at what event time, and were formal validity and third-party rights preserved as HCCH Article 2(3) requires?
Which overriding mandatory rules or public policy of the forum or a closely connected State limit the chosen law, and does the forum allow non-State rules of law in court as well as in arbitration?

If CISG governs and a matter is not settled in it, which general CISG principles or residual applicable law fill the gap, and how is that residual law identified without treating the choice-of-court clause as a choice of law?

layers.name: Parties, capacity and consent
layers.description: Bind two or more party positions to the agreement and link each position to a real person or organization and to signing authority.

findings.name: Party positions, places of business and authority
findings.description: CISG Article 1 looks to places of business, not nationality, and Article 10 selects the place of business with the closest relationship to the contract and its performance, or habitual residence if there is no place of business. UNIDROIT Article 2.1.1 treats agreement of the parties as sufficient to conclude a contract, including by conduct. LegalRuleML models Agent, Figure, Role, Bearer and Authority separately from the natural-language source. A party position (buyer, seller, guarantor, licensor) is therefore not the organization or person; it is a role filled by an actor, with signing capacity verified against a charter or agency sibling rather than stored as a full corporate record here. HCCH Article 1(3) keeps natural-person capacity and external agency out of choice-of-law principles, so those questions remain referenced, not duplicated.

questions.text: Which party positions exist on this agreement, what role does each play, and to which organization or person referent does each position point?
What is each party's relevant place of business or habitual residence, and which establishment has the closest relationship to the contract and its performance?
Who signed or otherwise manifested assent for each position, in what capacity, and which charter, power of attorney or agency instrument is referenced as the authority check?
Do the parties hold the agreement record jointly, and is any party a mere disclosed agent, undisclosed principal, or guarantor rather than a primary obligor?

layers.description: Record offer, acceptance, counter-offer and any writing or signature that the applicable law or the parties require.

findings.name: Offer, acceptance, conduct and battle of forms
findings.description: CISG Articles 14–24 and UNIDROIT Articles 2.1.1–2.1.14 define formation. A proposal is an offer if sufficiently definite and intended to be binding; it becomes effective when it reaches the offeree; it may be withdrawn before it reaches, and may be revoked until acceptance is dispatched unless stated irrevocable or reasonably relied upon. Acceptance is a statement or conduct indicating assent; silence is not in itself acceptance; it is effective when it reaches the offeror, or when a permitted act is performed. A purported acceptance with material modifications is a counter-offer; non-material modifications become part of the contract unless the offeror objects without undue delay. CISG Article 19(3) treats price, payment, quality, quantity, delivery, liability and dispute settlement as material. UNIDROIT Article 2.1.1 also allows conclusion by conduct sufficient to show agreement, including automated contracting systems the parties have agreed to operate. Writings in confirmation and terms left open are distinct from acceptance (UNIDROIT 2.1.12 and 2.1.14). The contract is concluded when acceptance becomes effective (CISG Article 23).

questions.text: When did the offer reach the offeree, when was acceptance dispatched and when did it reach the offeror, and at what event time was the contract concluded, as distinct from when those communications were ingested into the record?
Did any reply add or change terms, were those terms material under CISG Article 19(3) or the circumstances, and did the offeror object without undue delay?
Was the contract concluded by performance or other conduct without an identifiable offer and acceptance, or by an agreed automated system, and what conduct is sufficient to show agreement?
Was the offer stated to be irrevocable or reasonably relied upon, and did a revocation reach the offeree before acceptance was dispatched?

findings.name: Writing, electronic form and signature
findings.description: CISG Article 11 says a contract of sale need not be in writing and may be proved by any means, but Articles 12 and 96 allow a Contracting State whose law requires writing to restore a writing rule that the parties may not derogate from. CISG Article 13 includes telegram and telex in 'writing'. UCC § 2-201 makes a contract for sale of goods for $500 or more unenforceable unless there is a writing signed by the party against whom enforcement is sought, with merchant-confirmation, specially manufactured goods, admission and part-performance exceptions. UNCITRAL MLEC supplies functional equivalence for electronic information and writing; MLES supplies reliability criteria for electronic signatures. UNIDROIT Article 2.1.13 allows a party to insist that no contract exists until agreement is reached in a particular form. These rules conflict: the model must store the form actually used, the signature method, any Article 96 reservation, and whether a no-contract-until-formal-document stipulation was insisted upon.

questions.text: Does CISG Article 11 apply, has an Article 96 declaration restored a writing requirement, or does a domestic statute such as UCC § 2-201 require a signed writing, and which exception if any makes the agreement enforceable without it?
How was assent signed or otherwise authenticated, which reliability criteria under the UNCITRAL Model Law on Electronic Signatures were met, and which party position is bound by each signature?
Did a party insist that the contract is not concluded until a particular form or final document is executed, and has that form been completed?
If the record is electronic, which functional-equivalence rules treat it as writing and as a signature, and is any paper original still the controlling manifestation?

layers.name: Clause architecture
layers.description: Map hierarchical provisions, standard terms and negotiated text with stable citation paths.

findings.name: Provision hierarchy, standard terms and isomorphism
findings.description: Akoma Ntoso models hierarchical legal documents with nested sections, citation, FRBR versions and a strong split between authorial text and editorial metadata. LegalRuleML requires isomorphism between rules and their legal sources so that multiple rules may sit in one provision and several provisions may feed one rule. Commercial agreements therefore need addressable clauses with citation paths, clause class, source hash or text, and a flag for standard versus negotiated terms. UNIDROIT formation comments treat battle of standard terms and writings in confirmation as how standard terms enter the contract. A clause is not an obligation; it is the textual source from which deontic statements are derived.

questions.text: What is the stable citation path and identifier of each addressable provision, and which parent hierarchy does it sit in?
Which terms are standard terms of one party and which were negotiated, and did those standard terms become part of the contract through acceptance, confirmation or usage?
Which formal LegalRuleML or equivalent statements are isomorphic to which textual provisions, including many-to-many links?
Which expression of the instrument contains this clause after amendment, and is editorial markup distinguished from authorial text?

layers.name: Meaning
layers.description: Record interpretive materials: intent, usages, practices and good faith.

findings.name: Interpretation, usages and subsequent conduct
findings.description: CISG Article 8 interprets statements and conduct first by a party's intent where the other party knew or could not have been unaware of it, otherwise by a reasonable person of the same kind in the same circumstances, having regard to negotiations, practices, usages and subsequent conduct. Article 9 binds parties to agreed usages and established practices and, unless otherwise agreed, to international trade usages they knew or ought to have known. Article 7 requires interpretation of the Convention itself with regard to international character, uniformity and good faith. UNIDROIT Chapter 4 (as part of PICC 2016) supplies complementary interpretation and gap-filling. These materials are evidence for meaning, not a second contract.

questions.text: For a disputed statement or clause, did the other party know or could it not have been unaware of the speaker's intent, and if not what would a reasonable person of the same kind have understood?
Which agreed usages, established practices between the parties, or widely known international trade usages are implied into the contract unless excluded?
What subsequent conduct of the parties is to be considered in interpretation, and which negotiation records are in the interpretation file rather than in the four corners of the instrument?

layers.name: Commitments

findings.name: Obligations, permissions, prohibitions and conditions
findings.description: LegalRuleML distinguishes constitutive statements from prescriptive statements and models Obligation (a bearer is legally bound; non-performance is a Violation), Permission, Prohibition, Right (permission on the bearer implying duties on an auxiliary party), Penalty and Reparation. CISG Article 30 requires the seller to deliver goods, hand over documents and transfer property as required; Article 53 requires the buyer to pay the price and take delivery. Conditions, warranties and representations in common-law drafting are classifications of those duties, not a separate UN instrument. Each obligation in this model arises from one or more clauses, is owed by a party position, may be due on a date or on a condition, and has a performance status. Property transfer remains a CISG seller duty as between the parties but proprietary effect on third parties is out of scope.

questions.text: Is each commitment an obligation, permission, prohibition or right, who is the bearer and who if anyone is the auxiliary party?
From which clauses does the duty arise, what due condition or time makes it performable, and what is its current performance status?

For a sales contract, are the CISG Article 30 seller duties to deliver, hand over documents and transfer property, and the Article 53 buyer duties to pay and take delivery, all instantiated as obligations or has a party derogated from them?

findings.name: Milestones, place of performance, price and payment
findings.description: CISG Article 33 requires delivery on a fixed date, within a fixed period, or within a reasonable time. Article 31 sets default place of delivery. Article 55 supplies a reasonable price if none is determined. Articles 57–59 set place and time of payment and provide that the buyer must pay without request on the date fixed. UNIDROIT formation allows terms, including price, to be left open if an alternative means of determination exists (Article 2.1.14). Milestones and acceptance criteria are the operational schedule attached to obligations; they are not themselves the contract. Instalment contracts are recognised in CISG Article 73.

questions.text: What date, period or reasonable-time rule governs each performance, and at which place must delivery or other performance occur?
What price, currency and determination method apply, and if the contract is silent does CISG Article 55 or another gap-filler supply the price generally charged at conclusion?
Where and when must payment be made, is a request or formality required, and which invoice or documentary conditions precede payment?
What acceptance criteria attach to each milestone or deliverable, and which obligations does that milestone pace?

findings.name: Delivery, examination, conformity and acceptance
findings.description: CISG Article 35 requires goods of the quantity, quality and description in the contract, fit for ordinary or particular purpose, matching sample or model, and packaged as required. Articles 38–40 require examination in as short a period as practicable and notice of lack of conformity within a reasonable time and at latest two years from handover unless inconsistent with a guarantee; the seller cannot rely on late notice if it knew of the lack of conformity. Articles 37 and 48 give the seller rights to cure before and after the delivery date on stated conditions. LegalRuleML Compliance marks an obligation fulfilled or a prohibition not violated. Acceptance and rejection are party acts that discharge or refuse discharge of an obligation and must be stored with evidence and event time.

questions.text: Did the goods or other performance match the required quantity, quality, description, purpose, sample and packaging, and what examination was done and when?
Was lack of conformity notified within a reasonable time and within any two-year or guarantee limit, and has the counterparty accepted, rejected or taken delivery under reservation?
Did the performing party cure missing quantity, replacement or repair before or after the due date without unreasonable inconvenience or expense, and did the receiving party retain a damages claim?
What evidence record discharges or refuses the obligation, at what performance event time, and when was that evidence ingested?

findings.name: Passing of risk, impediment and hardship
findings.description: CISG Articles 66–70 pass risk on handover to the first carrier, on goods sold in transit, or on taking over, but not before identification to the contract. Article 79 exempts a party from damages if failure is due to an impediment beyond control that could not reasonably have been taken into account or overcome; the exemption lasts while the impediment exists; notice of the impediment is required; other rights than damages remain. Article 80 bars a party from relying on a failure it caused. UNIDROIT PICC 2016 additionally treat hardship for long-term contracts as a distinct adaptation or termination path; that is an alignment, not a CISG rule. Force majeure certificates and sanctions-related impediments are evidence of Article 79 or hardship, not a separate ontology, unless a specialised public-law model is referenced.

questions.text: Has risk passed, by which CISG Article 67–69 event, and were the goods clearly identified to the contract before risk could pass?
Is a failure excused under CISG Article 79 as an impediment beyond control, was notice given in reasonable time, and is the exemption limited to damages for the period of the impediment?
If UNIDROIT hardship or an equivalent clause applies, has a party requested renegotiation, adaptation or termination, and is that path distinct from CISG Article 79 exemption?
Did the claiming party's own act or omission cause the other party's failure so that CISG Article 80 bars reliance on that failure?

findings.name: Amendment, waiver and form of modification
findings.description: CISG Article 29 allows modification or termination by mere agreement, but a written contract requiring written modification may not otherwise be modified; a party may be precluded by conduct from asserting that clause to the extent the other party has relied on the conduct. Akoma Ntoso models active and passive modifications and versioning of legal texts, which maps to an amendment expression of the agreement. Each amendment needs an effective time, affected clauses, and a new expression identity. Waiver and estoppel are conduct-based and must not be collapsed into a formal amendment when CISG Article 29(2) second sentence applies.

questions.text: What identifier and new expression IRI does this amendment have, which clauses does it change, and at what effective event time does the change operate?

findings.name: Breach, additional time, cure, suspension and anticipatory breach
findings.description: CISG Article 25 defines fundamental breach as detriment that substantially deprives the other party of what it is entitled to expect, unless the result was not foreseeable. Articles 47 and 63 allow a Nachfrist additional period of reasonable length; during it the fixing party may not resort to inconsistent remedies but keeps damages for delay. Articles 71–72 allow suspension for apparent future non-performance of a substantial part, with immediate notice and a duty to continue if adequate assurance is provided, and avoidance for clear future fundamental breach. Article 73 deals with instalments. LegalRuleML Violation, Suborder, Penalty and Reparation model the deontic consequence of breach. A breach declaration is a party event, not a court judgment; adjudication is a sibling process.

questions.text: Has a party declared a breach, is it fundamental under CISG Article 25, and was the detriment foreseeable to a reasonable person in the same circumstances?
Has an additional period of reasonable length been fixed, what is its end time, and has the non-performing party offered cure that must be allowed to run?
Has performance been suspended for apparent future non-performance or avoided for clear future fundamental breach, was notice given, and was adequate assurance provided?
If the contract is an instalment contract, does the breach justify avoidance of one instalment, of future instalments, or of interdependent past deliveries as well?

layers.name: Remedies and end

findings.name: Damages, price reduction, avoidance, restitution and limitation
findings.description: CISG Articles 45–52 and 61–65 list buyer and seller remedies; damages may be claimed with other remedies. Article 28 lets a court refuse specific performance if it would not grant it under its own law. Articles 74–77 measure damages as foreseeable loss including lost profit, substitute-transaction and current-price differentials, subject to mitigation. Article 50 allows proportionate price reduction. Article 78 grants interest on sums in arrears. Articles 49 and 64 plus 26 require notice of avoidance; Articles 81–84 release future obligations, preserve dispute-settlement and winding-up clauses, and require concurrent restitution and accounting for benefits. LegalRuleML Penalty and Reparation link sanctions to violated prescriptions. UNIDROIT Chapter 10 limitation periods are a separate time-bar overlay; CISG itself does not set a general limitation period, and the 1974 Limitation Convention is a related but distinct instrument. Liquidated damages versus penalty enforceability is a validity-adjacent national conflict and must not be treated as uniformly enforceable.

questions.text: Which remedy is claimed or agreed: specific performance, repair or substitute goods, price reduction, damages, interest, agreed penalty or liquidated damages, or avoidance, and what is its status?
What foreseeable loss including lost profit is claimed, what substitute or current-price differential applies, and by how much must the claim be reduced for failure to mitigate?
Was avoidance declared by notice, which obligations are released, which dispute-settlement and winding-up clauses survive, and what concurrent restitution and benefit accounting is due?
Which limitation or prescription period applies, when did it start, has it been suspended, and does expiry bar the remedy without extinguishing the underlying right?
If specific performance is claimed, would the seized court grant it under its own law for similar domestic contracts as CISG Article 28 allows it to consider?

findings.name: Assignment, novation, guarantees and third-party rights
findings.description: HCCH Article 2(3) protects third-party rights when choice of law is modified. HCCH Article 1(3) excludes proprietary effects, insolvency and external agency from choice-of-law principles, so this model records only the contractual side: assignment of rights, transfer of obligations by agreement (novation), guarantees and expressly conferred third-party rights. UNIDROIT PICC 2016 contain chapters on assignment, transfer of obligations, assignment of contracts, set-off and plurality of obligors; those are alignments for data shape, not a claim that every jurisdiction treats assignment the same. A guarantor is a party position, not a new contract type, unless a separate guarantee instrument is itself an agreement instance.

questions.text: Which rights or obligations were assigned or novated, from which party position to which assignee, and was consent of the remaining party required and given?
Is there a guarantor party position or a separate guarantee agreement, and did the contract confer enforceable rights on a named third-party beneficiary?
Was the obligor notified of the assignment at what event time, and has any set-off been claimed against the assigned right?

layers.name: Process and record

findings.name: Notices, dispute clauses, joint record, access and retention
findings.description: CISG Articles 24, 26 and 27 define when a communication reaches a party and when delay in transmission does not deprive a party of the right to rely on it; avoidance requires notice. HCCH Principles distinguish choice of law from choice of court and arbitration agreements, which remain contractual terms but are excluded from the Principles' own scope. Akoma Ntoso lifecycle, workflow and preservation metadata support long-term records. UNCITRAL MLEC supports electronic notices as functional equivalents. The previous-version contracts remain operative as governance: each party holds a full mirror and joint facts change only by joint events; consented limited disclosure of existence and performance standing may be given to credit consumers; a dispute forum obtains access only once a dispute is escalated. Retention follows limitation periods, regulatory holds and the parties' agreed archive period; deletion of the joint record is not a unilateral CRUD delete.

questions.text: By what method and to which address must notices be given, when did a given notice reach the addressee under CISG Article 24, and is delayed transmission still effective under Article 27?
Does the agreement choose arbitration, a court, or another forum, what is the seat or venue and rules, and is that clause treated as severable from the main contract and from the choice of law?
Who holds a full mirror of the joint record, what consented disclosures of existence or performance standing are in force, and has adjudication access been opened by escalation?

What retention period and legal holds apply to the agreement record and evidence, and by what joint or legally compelled method may a record be deleted, redacted or archived after the limitation period?
Is the agreement record jointly owned by the party positions, and which stewardship or access-grant sibling objects implement grants beyond the party mirrors?

composition.purpose: Each contract party position that is not a natural person points to an organization as the real party; the agreement does not store the organization's legal personality, officers or identifiers as master data.
Natural-person parties and human signatories are person referents; capacity of natural persons is excluded from HCCH Principles Article 1(3)(a) and is not duplicated here.
A procurement award concludes in a new agreement instance here; tender process, evaluation and standstill remain in procurement and need not read clause text.
An insurance policy is a specialised commercial agreement; underwriting, coverage and claims operations extend this model rather than flattening a policy into a generic sale of goods.
Executed agreements may serve as price observations or as CISG Article 55 and 76 current-price inputs under a contribution contract; valuation methodology stays in the price model.
Signing capacity is verified against recorded powers; this model stores only the authority instrument reference on the party position.

Choice of court and arbitration clauses are terms of the agreement; HCCH Principles exclude those agreements from choice-of-law scope, and hearing, award and enforcement belong to the dispute-resolution model.
Joint ownership of the agreement record is a stewardship fact implemented by the catalogue stewardship model rather than by inventing a second owner type.
Disclosures to credit consumers and adjudication access are grants over the shared record, not new contract types.
Execution, performance, amendment, breach and access events require audit facets mixed in rather than a bespoke logging ontology.

CISG is the primary binding uniform sales code for in-scope international sales; alignment is not automatic application, because parties may exclude it and many commercial contracts are not sales of goods.

UNIDROIT PICC 2016 supply the general commercial vocabulary, including formation by conduct, automated contracting, writings in confirmation, hardship and limitation, and may be chosen as rules of law under HCCH Article 3.
LegalRuleML is the deontic and isomorphism overlay for obligations, permissions, prohibitions, violation, penalty and reparation derived from clause text.
Akoma Ntoso supplies document identity, hierarchy, citation, versioning and preservation metadata for the instrument without making XML the semantic model.
HCCH Principles govern how a choice of law is recorded and limited; they are non-binding best-practice principles, not a convention.
UCC § 2-201 is the competing US writing rule; other Article 2 doctrines are noted as a regional overlay and not fetched as canonical global rules.
MLEC and MLES supply functional equivalence for electronic records and signatures used in formation and notices.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension may add a UUID or ULID only after an authoritative master-system identifier and any governed IRI are recorded.
Identity creation must mint or bind an authoritative master-system identifier before a Dimension UUID or ULID is used alone.
Each contracting party holds a full mirror of the joint agreement record, and joint facts change only by jointly authorized events.
dimension.namespace_guidance: The registry namespace for this entry is vr.wm-eco-006 with model id WM-ECO-006; instrument markup reuses the Akoma Ntoso namespace http://docs.oasis-open.org/legaldocml/ns/akn/3.0 rather than minting a private legal-document vocabulary.

canonicalization_rules: Clause text is stored as canonical text plus a content hash.
Timestamps use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z, with event time stored separately from observation or ingestion time.
patch_rules: Clause text updates only by amendment that produces a new expression IRI; in-place silent edits are forbidden.
Joint facts change only by jointly authorized events or amendments, not by a unilateral write.
Unilateral hard delete of the joint record is forbidden; retention, legal hold and limitation clocks govern archive and redaction.
compatibility_rules: Projections may omit clause text but must not silently rewrite identity, status or amounts.
A prior expression remains historically addressable after an amendment.
Alignment to a standard is not a conformance claim for any particular agreement instance.

identity_priority: UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Timestamps use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z. Record event time, meaning when the legal or operational event such as reach of an acceptance, notice of avoidance or performance actually occurred, separately from observation or ingestion time when the record was observed or ingested, whenever those differ.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts such as registers, ledgers, dockets and event logs are named by the agreement expression they belong to; each amendment produces a new expression IRI rather than renaming or overwriting a prior expression entry.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Each contracting party holds a full mirror of the joint agreement record. Clause text is stored as canonical text plus a content hash. Joint facts change only by jointly authorized events. Projections may omit clause text but must not silently rewrite identity, status or amounts.

policies: Party-mirror policy: each party holds the full agreement record; joint facts change only by joint events or jointly authorized amendments.

Form-and-signature policy: writing and signature requirements follow the applicable instrument (CISG Articles 11–13 and 96, UCC § 2-201, MLEC/MLES) and any insisted particular form under UNIDROIT Article 2.1.13.
Disclosure-minimisation policy: existence and performance standing may be disclosed to consented credit or rating consumers; clause text and prices are omitted from public summaries.
No-unilateral-delete policy: the joint record is not deleted by a single party's CRUD delete; retention, legal hold and limitation clocks govern archive and redaction.

read: A party mirror may read the full record including clause text, hashes, performance evidence and amendment history.
A consented credit or rating consumer may read only existence, party names or identifiers, subject-matter class and a coarse performance-standing flag.
A dispute forum may read the record after adjudication access is opened by escalation.
Public summary projections may read existence, parties and subject-matter class and must omit terms and amounts.
create: A new agreement instance is created by conclude-agreement when formation rules are met, including from a procurement award compose.
Performance records, notices, breach declarations and amendment expressions are created as child events, not as new unrelated contracts.
Identity creation must mint or bind an authoritative master-system identifier before a Dimension UUID or ULID is used alone.
update: Status, obligation performance and remedy fields update only through recorded events with event time and ingestion time.
Clause text updates only by amendment that produces a new expression IRI; in-place silent edits are forbidden.
Choice of law may be modified at any time subject to HCCH Article 2(3) protection of formal validity and third-party rights.
delete: Unilateral hard delete of the joint record is forbidden.
After retention and limitation periods, parties may jointly archive or redact personal data in projections while preserving integrity hashes of the legal expression.
Legal holds from pending dispute, regulatory order or insolvency overlay suspend deletion.

roles.name: contracting-party
responsibilities: Hold a full mirror of the joint record
Manifest offer, acceptance, performance, notice, amendment consent and avoidance
Authorise consented disclosures of existence or standing

roles.name: authorized-signatory
responsibilities: Execute or otherwise authenticate the instrument within recorded capacity
Bind a party position without becoming a party in their own right unless also named

roles.name: contract-administrator
responsibilities: Ingest performance evidence, invoices, notices and milestone status
Keep event time distinct from observation or ingestion time
Maintain obligation ledger and amendment register

roles.name: adjudicator
responsibilities: Receive adjudication access only after escalation
Apply chosen law, CISG or PICC as aligned, and forum mandatory rules
Must not rewrite the joint party mirrors except through recognised award effects in a sibling model

roles.name: consented-status-consumer
responsibilities: Consume existence and performance-standing projections only within grant scope
Must not infer terms, prices or liability from the public summary

access.default_rule: Deny all non-party access to clause text, prices, performance evidence and personal signatory data; each contracting party has full read of its mirror.
exceptions: Adjudication access after a dispute is escalated to the contractual forum
Consented counterparty-status disclosure of existence and coarse performance standing to credit or rating consumers
Public-summary projection of existence, parties and subject-matter class where a transparency register is agreed or required
Mandatory regulatory disclosure that is an overriding mandatory rule of the forum
audit_requirements: Log execution, amendment, performance acceptance, breach declaration, avoidance, assignment and every access exception with actor, artifact, event time and ingestion time in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z
Preserve content hashes of each expression so that later projections can be verified
Record who opened adjudication access and under which dispute-clause identifier

coverage.claim: This research specifies a format-neutral commercial-contract meta-model sufficient for an agent to identify, form, interpret, perform, change and wind up a B2B agreement as a jointly owned record, aligned to CISG, UNIDROIT PICC 2016, LegalRuleML, Akoma Ntoso, HCCH choice-of-law principles, UCC § 2-201 and UNCITRAL electronic commerce and signature model laws. It does not claim a single global code of validity, property, insolvency or consumer protection, and it does not treat a contract as an organization.

checklist.notes: Master-system identifier, IRI and Dimension UUID or ULID, plus Akoma Ntoso FRBR work/expression/manifestation/item and content hashes.
Formation, performance, amendment, breach, cure, avoidance or termination and limitation clocks, including automated contracting and writings in confirmation.
Party positions to actors, obligations to clauses and bearers, milestones to duties, amendments to expressions, remedies to breaches, assignments to remaining parties.
Offer reach, acceptance dispatch and reach, due dates, Nachfrist, examination and notice windows, two-year conformity cut-off, limitation periods; RFC 3339 event versus ingestion time.
Negotiation history, subsequent conduct, signature packs, performance evidence and interpretation file; LegalRuleML authorial tracking and Akoma Ntoso author versus editor split.
Joint party-mirror ownership of the record; guarantor and third-party beneficiary distinguished from primary parties.
CISG Article 4 excludes validity; mistake, fraud, duress, unconscionability and illegality are not given a first-party uniform schema. Marked as overlay, not canonical.
Default deny to non-parties; party mirrors; consented status disclosure; adjudication access; public summary projection.
Retention tied to limitation periods and legal holds; unilateral delete forbidden; archive and redaction after clocks expire.

Alignments to CISG, PICC, LegalRuleML, Akoma Ntoso, HCCH Principles, UCC § 2-201, MLEC and MLES; sibling references for organization, person, procurement, insurance, price, charter, dispute, stewardship and audit.
CISG Part II and UNIDROIT Chapter 2 including battle of forms, late acceptance, terms left open and automated contracting.
LegalRuleML operators plus CISG seller and buyer core duties.
Damages, price reduction, interest, specific performance with Article 28 forum filter, avoidance, restitution, penalty/reparation overlay.
HCCH Principles Articles 1–3 and 11; dépeçage; non-State rules of law; mandatory-rule limits.

known_omissions: National validity doctrines (mistake, fraud, duress, unconscionability, illegality, consideration in common law) lack a uniform primary schema because CISG Article 4 excludes validity.

UCC Article 2 battle of forms (§ 2-207), adequate assurance (§ 2-609) and remedy catalogue were not fetched as live primary text beyond § 2-201; they are regional competitors to CISG, not canonical nodes.

UNIDROIT hardship, set-off, plurality of obligors, assignment chapters and limitation Chapter 10 are aligned from the 2016 instrument as a whole; individual articles beyond formation Chapter 2 were not re-fetched in this run.
The 1974 Limitation Convention (as amended 1980) is a related sales time-bar treaty and is not modelled as a first-class bundle.
Industry standard forms (ISDA Master, FIDIC, GAFTA, BIMCO) and clickwrap or platform terms of service are profiles, not core findings.
Smart-contract bytecode, oracles and on-chain settlement have only UNIDROIT automated-contracting comment support and remain an evidence gap.
Supervening sanctions, export controls and COVID-era hardship practice are public-law or factual overlays without a dedicated primary contract schema here.
eIDAS qualified-signature levels and UETA state enactments were not fetched; MLES is the cross-border alignment used instead.
PECL and the Draft Common Frame of Reference were not fetched live and are not treated as canonical.
Data-processing addenda, ESG clauses and modern slavery warranties are emerging clause classes without a governing primary standard in the source set.
conflicts: CISG Article 11 (no writing required) conflicts with UCC § 2-201 (signed writing for $500+) and with CISG Articles 12 and 96 reservations that restore a writing rule the parties cannot derogate from.

CISG Article 16 makes offers generally revocable until acceptance is dispatched, with reliance and stated irrevocability exceptions; many civil-law systems treat a fixed-time offer as irrevocable. UNIDROIT Article 2.1.4 comment records this as historically irreconcilable and selects CISG's main rule.

CISG Article 19 material-alteration list is more rigid than UNIDROIT Article 2.1.11 comment, which makes materiality contextual; UCC § 2-207 (unfetched beyond awareness) is a third battle-of-forms regime.
CISG Article 28 lets a court refuse specific performance according to its own law; civil-law systems more readily order performance.
CISG Article 79 impediment is not UNIDROIT hardship; treating force majeure certificates as automatic exemption would be a false conformance claim.
HCCH Article 3 choice of non-State rules of law is commonly allowed in arbitration and often disallowed in State courts unless forum law says otherwise.

Agreed penalties may be unenforceable as penalties in some common-law systems while liquidated damages and civil-law contractual penalties are treated differently; LegalRuleML Penalty is a deontic link, not a guarantee of enforceability.

Akoma Ntoso is designed primarily for parliamentary, legislative and judicial documents; using it for private commercial contracts is an alignment of document mechanics, not a claim that Akoma Ntoso normatively governs private agreements.
regional_assumptions: International sales between CISG Contracting States default to CISG unless excluded; purely domestic US goods sales more often meet UCC Article 2, including the § 2-201 writing rule.
Rome I Regulation choice-of-law mechanics in the EU were not fetched; HCCH Principles are used as the cross-border alignment and expressly sit alongside Rome I as a non-binding guide.
Article 96 writing reservations (for example historically relevant for some CISG Contracting States) must be checked per party place of business rather than assumed absent.
Islamic finance, OHADA uniform acts and PRC Contract/Civil Code particularities are not included and would be regional extensions.
Places of business, not nationality, determine CISG internationality (CISG Articles 1(3) and 10).
The default operating picture is a B2B commercial agreement, including but not limited to international sales, rather than a consumer, employment or purely domestic consumer-protection regime.
Party-mirror joint ownership is the stewardship default: each party holds a full record and joint facts change only by joint events.
Where CISG and a domestic writing statute both claim to apply, the model records both rules and the Article 96 reservation state rather than silently preferring one.
Event time and observation or ingestion time are stored separately whenever a notice, acceptance or breach declaration is transmitted rather than contemporaneously logged.
Alignment to a standard is not a conformance claim for any particular agreement instance.
adversarial_checks: The registry validation flag that a contract is not an organization is honoured: party positions bind actors; the agreement is a joint record, not an O1 entity.
CISG was not generalised to services, consumer sales, validity or property; those exclusions are modelled as out-of-scope or sibling boundaries.
UNIDROIT PICC were not treated as automatically binding; they apply when chosen, used to interpret or supplement, or selected as HCCH Article 3 rules of law.
Choice of court and arbitration clauses are stored as terms and then handed to the dispute-resolution sibling; HCCH Principles' exclusion of those agreements from choice-of-law scope is respected.
A date is never used as an identifier; execution date is a temporal attribute beside master-system id, IRI and UUID or ULID.
Electronic signature reliability is aligned to MLES rather than inventing a vendor-specific PKI as the semantic model.
Public-summary and credit-standing projections were checked so they cannot leak clause text, prices or personal signatory data by default.
